mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in less than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (historical threshold), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) reflects weak labor market conditions that constrain consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in less than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 550.0 thousand units signals a contraction in the housing sector, which is a major driver of consumer demand and economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 550.0, the 5-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 index points indicates a slowdown in manufacturing and industrial output, which reduces corporate profits and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 90.0, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a monetary policy mistake that tightens financial conditions during labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in less than 50% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise consecutively, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in less than 50% of periods when both GDPC1 and INDPRO decline, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a high inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals aggressive central bank action that increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, CPIAUCSL > 2.5% does not result in negative 20-day forward returns (i.e., average return is positive or not significantly negative at p<0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 5.0%), strong payroll growth (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5.0%, PAYEMS growth does not lead to positive 5-day forward returns (i.e., average return is negative or not significantly positive at p<0.05).
